lessons.title: Letter shapes: start, middle and end (ب ت ث ن ي)
lessons.bigQuestion: Your name looks different in capitals and small letters, but it is still your name. Can a letter change its shape and stay the same letter?
objectives: To understand that Arabic letters change shape at the start, middle and end of a word
successCriteria: All: point to ب at the start, middle and end
Most: name ب ت ث ن ي by their dots
Some: read a joined word like بَتَ
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: learning to read Allah's Book, one letter at a time

hook.text: Your name looks different in capitals and small letters, but it is still your name. Can a letter change its shape and stay the same letter?
hook.a: Yes! Arabic letters change shape when they join, but keep their dots and sound.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (Al-'Alaq 96:1). Learning letters is the first step to reading the Qur'an.

starter.q: Which way do we read Arabic?
Say Bismillah! Which vowel is this: بَ?

teach.heading: One letter, four shapes
teach.note: Bismillah. Write all four on the board. The dot stays the same; only the joining line changes. Like joined handwriting.

teach.heading: The tooth family
teach.note: Same 'tooth' shape, different dots. Children say the dots aloud.

teach.heading: Read with me
teach.note: Point right to left. Children echo with mics on in turn.
cycle: Three friends say it in turn

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which letter has three dots on top?
check.why: ث has three dots above; ت has two; ن has one.

practice.q: Read: بَتَ, تَبَ, نَبَتَ
practice.model: I do: I start on the right. بَ (ba), تَ (ta): bata. Now تَبَ: ta-ba.

practice.q: Which letter has two dots below?

independent.q: Pupil PDF: trace ب in its four shapes, then circle the tooth letters in a row of joined letters. The teacher listens to today's group read بَتَ.
independent.a: Four shapes traced; ب ت ث ن ي circled.
independent.model: The teacher traces the first ب: alone, then start, middle, end.

independent.q: Extend: write بَتَ on your whiteboard.

exit.q: How many dots has ن?
exit.a: one

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Your name looks different in capitals and small letters, but it is still your name. Can a letter change its shape and stay the same letter?
exit.a: Yes! Arabic letters change shape when they join, but keep their dots and sound.

lessons.homework: Show someone at home ب in four shapes; tick the revision log after saying Al-Fatihah.
lessons.send: SEND: colour cards for the rule, extra listening turns. EAL: key words with meanings. Stretch: find a new example in a surah you know.

lessons.title: Joining families: ج ح خ, س ش, ص ض, ط ظ
lessons.bigQuestion: Brothers and sisters can look alike. Which Arabic letters look like brothers?
objectives: To understand that letters in the same family join in the same way and only their dots differ
successCriteria: All: point to ج ح خ at the start of a word
Most: say which family a letter belongs to
Some: read a word with two joined families, like سَجَدَ
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: learning to read Allah's Book, one letter at a time

hook.text: Brothers and sisters can look alike. Which Arabic letters look like brothers?
hook.a: ج ح خ look alike; so do س ش, ص ض, ط ظ. The dots tell them apart.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (Al-'Alaq 96:1). Learning letters is the first step to reading the Qur'an.

starter.q: Which letter has three dots on top?
Which shape is the start of ب?

teach.heading: Letter families
teach.note: Bismillah. Same body, different dots.

teach.heading: In the middle and at the end
teach.note: Show middle and end shapes. ج ح خ keep their bowl at the end.

teach.heading: Read with me
teach.note: Words: سَجَدَ (sajada), حَسَدَ (hasada), خَطَبَ (khataba).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which letter is in the jeem family?
check.why: ج ح خ are the jeem family.

practice.q: Read: سَجَدَ
practice.model: I do: right to left: سَ (sa), جَ (ja), دَ (da): sajada.

practice.q: Which has dots: ص or ض?

independent.q: Pupil PDF: colour each family a different colour, then read three joined words. The teacher listens to today's group.
independent.model: The teacher colours ج ح خ blue and reads سَجَدَ.

independent.q: Extend: write سَجَدَ on your whiteboard.

exit.q: ش has how many dots?
exit.a: three

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Brothers and sisters can look alike. Which Arabic letters look like brothers?
exit.a: ج ح خ look alike; so do س ش, ص ض, ط ظ. The dots tell them apart.

lessons.homework: Find ج and س in your Qaidah and show a grown-up; tick the revision log.

lessons.title: Letters that never join to the next: ا د ذ ر ز و
lessons.bigQuestion: Some people always hold hands with the person behind them, but not in front. Which Arabic letters 'hold hands' only one way?
objectives: To understand that six letters never join to the letter after them, so a word can have a gap
successCriteria: All: name the six letters that do not join after
Most: point to the gap after ا or د in a word
Some: read a word with a non-joiner, like دَرَسَ
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: learning to read Allah's Book, one letter at a time

keywords.def: a letter that does not join to the next letter

hook.text: Some people always hold hands with the person behind them, but not in front. Which Arabic letters 'hold hands' only one way?
hook.a: ا د ذ ر ز و: they join to the letter before, but never to the letter after.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (Al-'Alaq 96:1). Learning letters is the first step to reading the Qur'an.

starter.q: Which letter has two dots on top?
Which is the start shape of ه?

teach.heading: Six shy letters
bullets: ا د ذ ر ز و
Never join to the letter after
teach.note: Bismillah. Call them the 'shy letters'.

teach.heading: Look for the gap
teach.note: Point to each gap.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which letter never joins to the next letter?
check.why: د is one of the six: ا د ذ ر ز و.

practice.q: Read: دَرَسَ
practice.model: I do: دَ (da), then a gap because د does not join after. رَ (ra), gap again. سَ (sa): darasa.

practice.q: Which is a 'shy letter'?

independent.q: Pupil PDF: circle the six shy letters in a row of words, then read زَرَعَ. The teacher listens to today's group.
independent.model: The teacher circles the first: د in دَرَسَ.

independent.q: Extend: write وَرَدَ on your whiteboard.

exit.q: How many shy letters are there?
Back to our ponder: Some people always hold hands with the person behind them, but not in front. Which Arabic letters 'hold hands' only one way?
exit.a: ا د ذ ر ز و: they join to the letter before, but never to the letter after.

lessons.title: Reading joined words with short vowels

hook.text: You can now read letters and vowels. What is the next big step to reading the Qur'an?
hook.a: Reading joined words: putting shapes and vowels together.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (Al-'Alaq 96:1). Learning letters is the first step to reading the Qur'an.

starter.q: Which vowel is under the letter?

teach.heading: Shapes plus vowels
bullets: Look at the vowel on each
teach.note: Bismillah. Revise fathah ـَ, kasrah ـِ, dammah ـُ.

teach.heading: Read with me
teach.note: Real words from the Qaidah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: All three letters have fathah: ka-ta-ba.

practice.q: Read: جَلَسَ, عَلِمَ
practice.model: I do: جَ (ja) لَ (la) سَ (sa): jalasa. عَ ('a) لِ (li) مَ (ma): 'alima.

practice.q: Which vowel is on لِ?

independent.q: Pupil PDF: read five joined words to a grown-up or partner and tick each one. The teacher listens to today's group.
independent.model: The teacher reads the first word and ticks it.

independent.q: Extend: write كَتَبَ on your whiteboard.

exit.q: Read: «جَلَسَ»

exit.q: Back to our ponder: You can now read letters and vowels. What is the next big step to reading the Qur'an?

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween
lessons.title: Sukoon: the quiet letter
objectives: Know that sukoon means no vowel sound
Read letters with sukoon smoothly
Read short words with sukoon

keywords.def: a small circle that means the letter has no vowel

teach.heading: What is sukoon?
bullets: It means the letter is silent of vowels
We join its sound to the letter before
teach.note: Draw the circle. Say 'The letter has no vowel of its own; it leans on the letter before it.' Example: بَلْ - 'bal', not 'ba-la'.

teach.heading: Easy examples
teach.note: Read with the class; keep the sound short. Examples from the Qur'an: 'لَمْ' appears in Al-Ikhlas ('lam yalid'). Show the circle on top of the last letter.

teach.heading: Sukoon in the middle
teach.note: These have sukoon in the middle. Join the sukoon letter to the letter before: nā-'bu-du, not na-a-bu-du. Children often add an extra vowel; model correctly.

teach.heading: Qur'an words with sukoon
teach.note: These are from Surat Al-Ikhlas. Read them slowly. Note that the final letter of 'yalid' has sukoon. We will practise this surah later.

independent: Circle the sukoon in each word
exit: Draw a sukoon on a letter
lessons.homework: Find three words with sukoon on a page of your Qaidah and read them to someone.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: tap the table once for sukoon. Stretch: read longer words with two sukoons.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween
lessons.title: Shaddah: the strong letter
objectives: Know that shaddah doubles a letter
Read words with shaddah
Read shaddah words from the Qur'an

keywords.def: a mark like a small 'w' that doubles a letter

teach.heading: What is shaddah?
bullets: Shaddah looks like a small 'w' above the letter ّ
It means the letter is said twice
Press the letter firmly and hold it
teach.note: Shaddah = first sukoon, second with vowel. Example: رَبِّ = rab-bi. Tap the table twice for the two beats.

teach.heading: Reading shaddah
teach.note: Read each word slowly. Stress that the doubled letter sounds like a double tap. Common mistake: ignoring the shaddah. Praise accurate doubling.

teach.heading: Shaddah with kasrah
teach.note: In رَبِّ, the kasrah is placed below the letter even though shaddah is above. Read it as bbi. Show on the board.

teach.heading: Shaddah game
teach.note: Teacher reads a word either with or without shaddah (e.g. رَبَ vs رَبِّ). Children show one finger or two. Great for listening skills.

practice: How many times do we say a letter with shaddah?
exit: What does shaddah do to a letter?
lessons.homework: Find shaddah on a page of your Qur'an or Qaidah and show us its word.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: clap twice for shaddah. Stretch: explain the difference between بَ and بَّ.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween
lessons.title: Madd: long vowels (alif, waaw, yaa)
objectives: Know the three long vowel letters
Hold a madd for two counts
Read words with madd

keywords.def: stretching a sound for a fixed length
one beat; two counts is the normal madd

teach.heading: Three madd letters
bullets: و waaw with sukoon after dammah: buu
ي yaa with sukoon after kasrah: bee
teach.note: Write: بَا بُو بِي. The vowel before decides the letter: fathah before alif, dammah before waaw, kasrah before yaa. Say each sound long: two counts.

teach.heading: How long is two counts?
bullets: Not too short, not too long
teach.note: Teach counting with fingers. Stress that the sound is steady. Over-stretching and cutting short are both mistakes in tajweed.

teach.heading: Words from the Qur'an
teach.note: Read with two counts on each long vowel. Ask: which letter is the madd letter? In العالمين find the alif and the yaa.

teach.heading: Madd listening
bullets: Children show a fist (short) or open hand (long)
teach.note: Alternate between بَ and بَا, بُ and بُو. Ensure you model clearly. This builds the ear for tajweed in later years.

practice: How many counts is the madd?
independent: Underline the madd letter in each word
exit: Which letter follows a fathah to make a long sound?
lessons.homework: Tap out two counts while you say 'An-Naas' ten times.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use an arm swipe for the length. Stretch: read all madd words from Al-Fatihah.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween
lessons.title: Tanween: the 'n' ending
objectives: Know the three tanween marks
Read tanween words with the 'n' sound
Spot tanween in short surahs

keywords.def: two short vowel marks at the end of a word that add an 'n' sound

teach.heading: Tanween
teach.note: Tanween appears only at the end of a word. It means 'an' 'in' 'un'. Say with the class: baban, babin, babun (bāb with tanween). Show the doubled marks.

teach.heading: Reading examples
teach.note: The first two are from Surat Al-Ikhlas and Al-Asr. Read letter by letter. Remind: tanween is -un, -in, -an, never separated from the word.

teach.heading: Fathatayn and alif
bullets: Fathatayn often sits on a letter followed by alif
When we stop, we say a long aa instead
teach.note: At this stage say: when we stop on fathatayn, we say a long 'aa' instead of 'an'. We will study this later (madd 'iwad). Keep it simple.

teach.heading: Tanween sort
bullets: Say the mark and the sound
teach.note: Children sort cards. Teacher reads words aloud: which ending? Provide cards in both Arabic and transliteration for support.

independent: Sort word cards into three groups
Underline the tanween in a surah line
lessons.homework: Find tanween in Surat Al-Ikhlas (ayah 1) and tell someone what it says.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use colour for each tanween type. Stretch: write a sentence with a tanween word.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Reading and reciting short surahs
lessons.title: Reciting Al-Fatihah from the mushaf
objectives: Read all seven ayat of Al-Fatihah with the right marks
Say the letters from their correct places
Recite Al-Fatihah by heart

keywords.def: the Opening surah recited in every prayer
the places where letters come from

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3
teach.note: Read each ayah slowly. Notice shaddah in 'Rabbi' and 'Rahmaan', madd in 'aalameen'. Teacher reads, class echoes, then pairs read.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-5
bullets: You alone we worship and ask for help
teach.note: Each 'Iyyaaka' in ayah 5 has a shaddah and a madd. Hold the madd for two counts. Ask: what do we say to Allah in this ayah? Link to du'a.

teach.heading: Ayat 6-7
teach.note: Ayah 7 is long; chunk it as shown. Check 'an'amta' (sukoon on noon) and 'ad-daal-leen' (shaddah and madd). Praise clarity.

teach.heading: Recite without looking
bullets: Check each ayah with a partner
teach.note: Use a 'read-cover-say-check' routine. Children who struggle recite two ayat; those secure recite all seven. Record tracker scores.

practice: Where is the shaddah in ayah 5?
exit: What do we ask Allah for in this ayah?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fatihah to a family member and ask them to say Ameen at the end.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: allow reading support with the mushaf plus echo. Stretch: say Al-Fatihah with correct madd lengths and pauses.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Reading and reciting short surahs
lessons.title: Surat An-Nas
objectives: Read An-Nas with the right letters and marks
Know the meaning of ayat 1-3
Memorise An-Nas ayat 1-3

keywords.def: surah 114, six ayat, we seek Allah's protection

teach.heading: The surah
bullets: It is the last surah in the Qur'an
teach.note: Remind the class An-Nas is the last surah in the Qur'an. We seek Allah's protection in it. Show the page in the mushaf.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3
teach.note: Meaning: Say, I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind. Three names: Rabb, Malik, Ilah. Chunk and echo each ayah.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-6
teach.note: Meaning in brief: from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers in people's hearts, from jinn and people. Keep explanation short for age six. Link to seeking refuge with Allah when feeling bad thoughts.

teach.heading: Learn by chunks
teach.note: Teach the memory routine: listen x5, read x5, cover x5. Recite ayat 1-3 securely this lesson; 4-6 next lessons.

practice: What is the last surah in the Qur'an?
exit: What do we seek in An-Nas?
lessons.homework: Recite An-Nas ayat 1-3 to a family member every day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: slow chunking with echo. Stretch: recite ayat 4-6 as well.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Reading and reciting short surahs
lessons.title: Surat Al-Falaq
objectives: Read Al-Falaq with the right letters and marks
Know the meaning of ayat 1-2
Memorise Al-Falaq ayat 1-3

keywords.def: surah 113, five ayat, seek protection with the Lord of the daybreak

starter: Name the four types of marks you know.

teach.heading: Al-Falaq
teach.note: Explain that these two surahs are recited for protection. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite them (Sahih al-Bukhari). Keep the explanation light.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3
teach.note: Meaning: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles. Chunk and echo. Watch qaaf in Al-Falaq: make it from the back of the tongue.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-5
teach.note: Meaning: from the evil of those who blow on knots (practise magic), and from the evil of an envier when he envies. Mention that envy (hasad) is wrong. Keep it brief.

teach.heading: Practice and tracker
teach.note: Short, sharp repetition. Record who has ayat 1-3 secure. Use stickers on the tracker.

exit: What are An-Nas and Al-Falaq for?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Falaq ayat 1-3 and An-Nas ayat 1-3 before bed this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pictures for daybreak and darkness. Stretch: recite all five ayat.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Ikhlas, Al-Masad and joining letters
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4: Allah has no child, no parent and no equal
lessons.bigQuestion: Everyone you know has a mother or father. Allah is different. How?
objectives: To memorise Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: say 112:3 to 4 after the teacher
Most: say all of Al-Ikhlas alone
Some: say what 112:4 teaches about Allah
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: Allah is unique; nothing is like Him

hook.text: Everyone you know has a mother or father. Allah is different. How?
hook.a: Allah has no child and no parent, and nothing is like Him (112:3 to 4).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent' (Al-Ikhlas 112:3 to 4). The Prophet ﷺ said Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Qur'an (Bukhari).

starter.q: Recite Al-Ikhlas 112:1 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 112:3-4 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (٣) وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ (٤)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: English helps us understand; only the Arabic is the Qur'an
Big idea: nothing is like Allah
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: He neither begets nor is born,
Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 112:3-4 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Mics on in turn: three friends repeat

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: 112:4: there is none equal to Him.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 with the teacher.
practice.model: I do: chunk 112:3-4. Ayah 3: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 4 the same way. Then link: recite 3 and 4 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening turns: today's group says 112:3-4 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: Say the whole of Al-Ikhlas to a friend.

exit.q: Al-Ikhlas 112:3: «لَمْ يَلِدْ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: وَلَمْ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Everyone you know has a mother or father. Allah is different. How?
exit.a: Allah has no child and no parent, and nothing is like Him (112:3 to 4).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 to a parent three times a day and revise Al-Ikhlas 112:1 to 2 and Al-Fatihah; tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: one ayah at a time, extra listening turns, finger tracking on the pupil PDF. EAL: key words shown with meanings. Stretch: lead the echo for a group.

keywords.def: sincerity: the name of the surah

hook.text: If someone asked you 'Who is Allah?', what would you say?
hook.a: Allah is One (112:1); everyone needs Him and He needs no one (112:2).

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said Surat Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Qur'an (Bukhari). Allah says: 'Say, He is Allah, the One' (Al-Ikhlas 112:1).

starter.q: Which surah do we say in every salah?
Which way do we read Arabic?
What do we say before we recite?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Ikhlas 112:1-2
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 112:1-2 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (١) ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ (٢)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: English helps us understand; only the Arabic is the Qur'an
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 112:1-2 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Mics on in turn: three friends repeat

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: أَحَدٌ means One: Allah is One.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Ikhlas 112:1-2 with the teacher.
practice.model: I do: chunk 112:1-2. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening turns: today's group says 112:1-2 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: Hold up one finger and say: 'Allah is One'.
independent.a: Pupil says it with one finger up.

exit.q: Al-Ikhlas 112:1 begins ...
exit.a: قُلْ هُوَ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: If someone asked you 'Who is Allah?', what would you say?
exit.a: Allah is One (112:1); everyone needs Him and He needs no one (112:2).
